name: PAM Triage — SOAR sketch
description: Stitches a CRITICAL-severity PAM-detector alert from Splunk SPL or Sentinel KQL into a five-task analyst-handoff workflow. Sketch — not validated against a live XSOAR tenant.

task.name: Fetch session details
task.description: Pulls the full PAM session record (commands, vault fetches, ticket metadata) from the upstream PAM platform via REST. Stub: a real deployment would call CyberArk PSM REST API endpoint /API/Recordings/${incident.session_id}.

task.name: Enrich user from HR
task.description: Looks up the privileged user's HR profile (department, manager, recent role changes) so the analyst sees organisational context next to the technical alert. Stub: real deployment maps to your SCIM / Workday / SailPoint integration.

task.name: CRITICAL severity?
task.description: Routes CRITICAL alerts (LLM confidence ≥ 0.92 AND ≥ 2 distinct rules fired — the same threshold the dashboard's risk algorithm uses) to Tier-2 with HIGH severity; everything else stays with Tier-1 at MEDIUM. Mirrors the dashboard explainer table verbatim.

task.name: Assign Tier-2 (HIGH)
task.description: Routes the incident to the Tier-2 SOC queue, raises severity to HIGH, posts a summary to the #soc-tier-2 Slack channel. Tier-2 closes the loop with a confirmed/false-positive verdict that becomes feedback for the next model retrain (see playbook gap below).

task.name: Assign Tier-1 (MEDIUM)
task.description: Default branch — Tier-1 SOC handles HIGH / MEDIUM / LOW alerts at MEDIUM severity. Tier-1 escalates to Tier-2 if needed; otherwise closes with their own verdict.

task.name: Wait for analyst verdict
task.description: End-of-sketch marker. A production playbook would here implement: (a) WaitForIncidentClosure with a 24-hour SLA timer, (b) on confirmed_true_positive → AutoRevokeVaultCredential + open follow-up case, (c) on false_positive → append to feedback queue feeding the quarterly model retrain. These three branches are the natural extension and are NOT in this stub.
